If you're not in a rush to get the latest Apple product on launch day and don't mind waiting a bit, Apple's officially certified refurbished product store has always been a reliable choice. Generally speaking, about three months after a new product goes on sale, the first batch of refurbished units will appear on Apple's website.

Other companies offer similar options, such as Amazon Renewed and Walmart Restored, but be aware that the standards they adopt and warranty terms are different...

Apple Certified Refurbished Products

Buying from the Apple Certified Refurbished Products store typically saves you around 15%, and the products are identical to brand-new units. Specifically, Apple promises all of the following:

  • Full inspection and testing performed by Apple
  • Brand new housing, so absolutely no scratches or wear
  • Brand new battery, so battery life is the same as a new unit
  • Comes with all original accessories and cables
  • Comes with Apple's standard one-year warranty, with the same coverage as a new unit
  • You can also purchase AppleCare+ additionally

Basically the only difference you'll see is that the product comes in a plain white box rather than the original packaging.

Amazon Renewed

Amazon Renewed is usually more competitively priced, but note that the product condition does not come with the same guarantees:

  • Inspection and testing performed by the seller rather than Apple
  • Used housing, so there will be scratches and wear (see below)
  • Used battery, only guaranteed to still have at least 80% of original capacity
  • Accessories may not be original Apple products
  • Comes with a 90-day Amazon warranty, rather than Apple's one-year warranty

Regarding scratches and wear, Amazon offers three quality grades:

  • Premium / Excellent: No wear visible when viewed from 12 inches away
  • Good: Minor scratches when viewed from 12 inches away, barely noticeable to the naked eye
  • Acceptable: Scratches easily seen and felt

Walmart Restored

Walmart Restored is even more vague than Amazon and doesn't clearly state what you're getting for your money:

  • No commitment whatsoever regarding cosmetic condition, only claims "performance and reliability like new"
  • No specific information provided on battery condition, only what's mentioned above
  • No information provided about accessories
  • Warranty provided by the seller, not Apple's one-year warranty

The Restored Premium tier comes with a one-year seller warranty, while Like New, Good, and Fair tiers only have 90 days. The company doesn't clearly define what each tier actually represents.

9to5Mac's Take

If you want a product that looks identical to a new unit and comes with an Apple warranty, the Apple Refurbished Store is clearly the first choice.

However, Amazon Renewed pricing can indeed be much cheaper, so if you're willing to accept the trade-offs mentioned above, it's still a pretty good deal. Especially if you listen to what we say and save money to upgrade to the iPhone 17 Pro instead of this year's new model (you're only missing one feature), there are indeed some attractive deals here:

  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,214 (original price $1,599) — All-time low price
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,215 (original price $1,599) — All-time low price
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,208 (original price $1,599) — All-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,164 (original price $1,299) — All-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,170 (original price $1,299) — All-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,171 (original price $1,299) — Only $1 more than the all-time low price

As for Walmart Restored, their promises are really too vague, I really don't have the confidence to say anything, but if you're not satisfied, you can always opt to return it.
